rows.answer:
No `jitless`/`allowsEval` usage in the legacy v3 code path — this is v4-only. The fix and full test run are complete.

## Summary

**Root cause**: In `$ZodObjectJIT` (`packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts`), the `jitless` check was computed **once**, at schema-construction time, and frozen into a closure (`const jit = !core.globalConfig.jitless; const fastEnabled = jit && allowsEval.value;`). Since schemas are typically defined at module scope before an app gets around to calling `z.config({ jitless: true })` at startup, that config change had no effect on already-constructed schemas — their `.parse()` calls kept invoking `new Function(...)` (via `util.allowsEval` and via `doc.compile()` in `generateFastpass`), tripping the CSP `unsafe-eval` restriction regardless of the later config call.

**Fix**: Check `core.globalConfig.jitless` (and per-call `ctx.jitless`) live inside `inst._zod.parse` on every call, and only touch `util.allowsEval.value` once jitless is confirmed off. This makes `z.config({ jitless: true })` effective no matter when it's called relative to schema creation, as long as it's set before `.parse()` runs.

Verified with a repro that proxies the global `Function` constructor to count eval attempts — before the fix, defining a schema and then calling `z.config({ jitless: true })` still triggered 2 eval calls on parse; after the fix, 0. Added a permanent regression test at `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/jitless-config.test.ts` (didn't touch existing test files, per instructions). Full suite: 329 files / 3699 tests pass.

rows.answer:
All 3764 tests pass across the entire zod package, no regressions.

## Summary

**Root cause**: in `$ZodTuple`'s parse loop (`packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts`), when the input array was shorter than the tuple's fixed length, any trailing item at/after the "optional zone" (`optStart`) was skipped via `continue` *before* its schema ever ran. This meant `.default()`-wrapped items in that trailing zone never got a chance to apply their default — the slot was just left empty, and consumers (like `ZodFunction.implement`, which validates each argument) then saw `undefined` where a required string was expected.

**Fix**: always run each item's parser (passing `undefined` for missing trailing input), so `$ZodDefault` gets to substitute its default value as designed. To preserve the pre-existing behavior for genuinely optional items (not shortening the output array when nothing is filled in), the result is only dropped from the output when it's a trailing slot, the parsed value is `undefined`, and there were no issues — i.e., truly nothing happened. If the schema produced a real value (default) or issues, it's assigned normally.

Verified with ad-hoc tests covering all three scenarios from the bug report (`z.tuple` with a defaulted trailing item, `.default()` on the whole tuple, and `z.function` with a defaulted parameter), plus edge cases mixing `.optional()` and `.default()` in the same tuple — all pass, and the full `packages/zod` suite (3764 tests) still passes with no regressions.

All 3774 tests pass (334 pre-existing files + the new one).

## Summary

**Root cause:** In `$ZodTuple`'s parse function (`packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts`), when the input array was shorter than the tuple's item list, indices in the trailing "optional" region (`i >= optStart`) were skipped entirely via `continue` — the item's schema parser was never invoked. This meant `$ZodDefault` wrappers (which need to actually *run* to substitute their default value) never got a chance to fire, so missing trailing tuple slots stayed `undefined` instead of picking up their default.

**Fix:** For indices past the input length that fall in the optional trailing region, the item's parser is now run with `value: undefined` (so `ZodDefault` can apply and `ZodOptional` still resolves to `undefined` as before). The result is only written into the output array when it resolves to something other than `undefined`, preserving the existing "trim trailing plain-optional slots" behavior for tuples with no defaults, while now correctly filling in defaults. Issues raised by the item's parser (e.g. a default value failing a `.refine()`) now correctly surface too.

Added `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/tuple-default.test.ts` covering: single/multiple missing trailing defaults, that plain optional (no default) trailing items are still omitted as before, that refinement errors on a default surface, and the exact `z.function` scenario from the bug report. Full `packages/zod` suite (3774 tests) passes.
